name: Phishing & Social Engineering
description: Phishing, social engineering, disinformation, and human-targeted deception.
narrative:
The earliest work in this thread treated phishing and social engineering as a measurement problem: where do attacks slip through, and why do people fall for them? "End-to-End Measurements of Email Spoofing Attacks" (2018) showed that email providers still struggled to reliably authenticate senders, leaving spear-phishing room to operate, and "Detecting and Characterizing Lateral Phishing at Scale" (2019) extended the lens to attacks that come from already-compromised internal accounts. Alongside the infrastructure view, a human-factors strand emerged — "Cognitive Triaging of Phishing Attacks" (2019) and "Users Really Do Answer Telephone Scams" (2019) quantified the psychological triggers and behaviors that make deception work.

The 2020-2021 period shifted toward studying the phishing ecosystem as a living system and toward building automated detectors. "Sunrise to Sunset: Analyzing the End-to-end Life Cycle and Effectiveness of Phishing Attacks at Scale" (2020) and "PhishTime" (2020) measured how attacks evolve over their lifespan and how well blacklists actually keep up. A major breakthrough came with "Phishpedia: A Hybrid Deep Learning Based Approach to Visually Identify Phishing Webpages" (2021), which made reference-based visual detection practical and explainable. Researchers also started gaming out the adversary's countermoves, as in "PhishPrint: Evading Phishing Detection Crawlers by Prior Profiling" (2021), recognizing that detectors and evaders co-evolve.

From 2022 onward the deep-vision, reference-based paradigm matured and was repeatedly hardened against real-world evasion. "Inferring Phishing Intention via Webpage Appearance and Dynamics" (2022) added interaction and intent, "Knowledge Expansion and Counterfactual Interaction for Reference-Based Phishing Detection" (2023) and "PhishDecloaker" (2024) closed gaps around limited reference lists and CAPTCHA-cloaked sites, while "TRIDENT" (2023) broadened the scope to web-based social engineering beyond credential phishing.

Most recently, large language models reshaped both attack and defense. "KnowPhish" (2024) and "Less Defined Knowledge and More True Alarms" (2024) folded LLMs and knowledge graphs into detection to escape brittle pre-defined reference lists, while "DeepPhish" (2022) had already flagged that AI-generated personas erode user trust. The frontier now includes LLMs as a new threat surface themselves — "LLM-Fuzzer: Scaling Assessment of Large Language Model Jailbreaks" (2024) and "Unsafe LLM-Based Search" (2025) study how AI systems can be manipulated or weaponized for deception, marking the field's pivot from defending humans against phishing pages to securing the AI intermediaries now sitting between users and the web.

milestones.title: End-to-End Measurements of Email Spoofing Attacks
milestones.note: established the measurement foundation by exposing how email providers still fail to authenticate spoofed senders

milestones.title: Detecting and Characterizing Lateral Phishing at Scale
milestones.note: broadened the threat model to phishing launched from already-compromised internal accounts

milestones.title: Sunrise to Sunset: Analyzing the End-to-end Life Cycle and Effectiveness of Phishing Attacks at Scale
milestones.note: framed phishing as an evolving lifecycle, revealing detection gaps that attacks exploit over time

milestones.title: Phishpedia: A Hybrid Deep Learning Based Approach to Visually Identify Phishing Webpages
milestones.note: made reference-based visual deep-learning detection practical and explainable, defining a dominant paradigm

milestones.title: Inferring Phishing Intention via Webpage Appearance and Dynamics: A Deep Vision Based Approach
milestones.note: advanced detection from static appearance to webpage dynamics and inferred intent

milestones.title: KnowPhish: Large Language Models Meet Multimodal Knowledge Graphs for Enhancing Reference-Based Phishing Detection
milestones.note: fused LLMs and knowledge graphs to overcome brittle pre-defined reference lists

milestones.title: LLM-Fuzzer: Scaling Assessment of Large Language Model Jailbreaks
milestones.note: marked the pivot to LLMs themselves as a manipulable deception surface

milestones.title: Unsafe LLM-Based Search: Quantitative Analysis and Mitigation of Safety Risks in AI Web Search
milestones.note: extended the field to securing AI search intermediaries now mediating users and the web
